    "200  Five Straight Losses, One Divergence: Where the Major Indexes Stand Now — TradingView News Search Products Community Markets Brokers More EN Get started News / PR Newswire / Five Straight Losses, One Divergence: Where the Major Indexes Stand Now Five Straight Losses, One Divergence: Where the Major Indexes Stand Now 5 min read QQQ CALGARY, AB, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Canada News Group News Commentary - Wall Street heads into Thursday's session with the S&P 500 on its longest losing streak since June. The benchmark fell 16.90 points, or 0.23%, on Wednesday to 7,323.63, its fifth straight decline, according to CNBC, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 101.50 points, or 0.42%, to 24,429.88 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 561.25 points, or 1.11%, to 50,198.17. Index funds that track the benchmarks in this commentary include: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE Arca: SPY) , SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE Arca: DIA) , Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ) , iShares Russell 2000 ETF (NYSE Arca: IWM) . The Scoreboard, as of Wednesday ' s Close Week-to-date figures compare Wednesday's close with the close on Friday, November 13. Year-to-date figures compare it with the December 31, 2025 close. Both are calculated from Associated Press closing data. S&P 500: 7,323.63. Week to date, down 238.04 points, or 3.15%. Year to date, up 478.13 points, or 6.98%. Dow Jones Industrial Average: 50,198.17. Week to date, down 2,149.38 points, or 4.11%. Year to date, up 2,134.88 points, or 4.44%. Nasdaq Composite: 24,429.88. Week to date, down 706.39 points, or 2.81%. Year to date, up 1,187.89 points, or 5.11%. Russell 2000: 2,742.94 at Monday's close, down 47.55 points, or 1.7%, on the day, after ending last week up 308.58 points, or 12.4%, for the year. Small caps finished higher on Wednesday. How the Week Has Unfolded Monday set the tone. The Nasdaq Composite fell 626.52 points, or 2.5%, to 24,509.76, and the S&P 500 fell 1.92% to 7,416.59 as technology stocks dropped sharply, according to the Associated Press and CNBC. On Tuesday, the selling shifted toward the Dow, which fell 848.75 points, while the S&P 500 lost 76.06 points, by our arithmetic from AP closing data. Wednesday split the indexes. Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, released in the afternoon, showed that almost all officials see further rate increases as likely appropriate, according to reports on the minutes, and Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC the central bank may need a half-point increase in December. A drop of about 10% in one heavyweight health insurer accounted for about two-fifths of the Dow's decline, according to FXStreet, while the Nasdaq Composite and the Nasdaq-100 finished higher. The Fed's next policy decision is scheduled for December 9, according to its meeting calendar. The pullback follows a stronger stretch. For the week ended Friday, November 13, the S&P 500 rose 184.81 points",
